items.title: Keralam: Muslims step in to help with two Hindu women's final rites
items.summary: Since childhood, Kalyani Amma has been simply "Amma" to Razak, now a 51-year-old. "She is not 'like my mother'; she is my mother," he says. It's a feeling shared by his younger brother Sulaiman. On November 7, when the 86-year-old died in Vaduvanchal, Wayanad, she had no children or living relatives. Razak and Sulaiman performed her last rites according to Hindu rites. Some 115 km away in Pallikkara, Malappuram, the Khadeeja mosque opened its doors for the last rites of another Hindu woman on November 10. Premalatha, 52, lived in a rented house too small for her body to be bathed and prepared for the final rites. The mosque offered its grounds instead. Both the incidents became headlines but it wasn't anything unusual for the people who were involved in it. For them, living together peacefully and offering support to neighbors is simply a normal way of life, rather than an extraordinary deed deserving public attention. ‘She is my mother’ Kalyani Amma worked multiple jobs to make a living; she had a cattle and used to do cleaning work at a private bank. items.title: After Arnab and Murasu, third cyclone ‘Akvan’ to hit Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm, named Akvan, by the evening of November 16 and further strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The system is moving north-northwestwards over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. It is expected to gather strength over the next two days and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. This would be the third cyclone to affect Andhra Pradesh in the past few weeks after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu caused extensive damage. The weather system intensified into a deep depression on November 15, when it was located about 640 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 760 km east-southeast of Chennai and 870 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam. Andhra Pradesh is also awaiting a central assessment of the damage caused by Cyclone Murasu and the subsequent financial aid from the BJP led Union government. Cyclone Murasu struck the state earlier this month. items.title: TN govt suspends five library officials over AI book scam
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government suspended five senior officials of the Directorate of Public Libraries, on Sunday, November 15, over alleged large-scale irregularities in the procurement of books for government libraries across the state. The alleged irregularities include the purchase of AI-generated publications, books containing fabricated information, fictitious author names and titles carrying questionable International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs). The suspensions were ordered by School Education Minister A Rajmohan, four days after the Madras High Court directed the state government to initiate disciplinary proceedings against officials allegedly involved in the irregularities and ordered the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to register an FIR. The suspended officials include S Kamatchi, Chief Librarian and Information Officer (in-charge) and Deputy Chief Librarian at Anna Centenary Library (ACL), Chennai; Dinesh Kumar, Chief Librarian and Information Officer (in-charge) at Kalaignar Centenary Library (KCL), Madurai; V Santhanakrishnan, Librarian and Information Officer at KCL, who also held additional charge of Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore; S Santh
